metadata.implementation: Wrap motion-heavy CSS animations (transforms, scaling, panning) in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference). metadata.implementation: Apply CSS 'text-align: right' (or utility classes like 'text-right') to both the <th> and <td> elements of columns containing numeric data such as currency, percentages, or counts. metadata.detect: Inspect table columns containing numbers. Verify that the computed style for text-align is right for both the header (<th>) and data cells (<td>).

metadata.implementation: Apply the CSS property scroll-padding-top to the html element or main scroll container, setting its value to the height of any fixed or sticky headers. metadata.anti_pattern: Implementing a fixed top navigation bar without adjusting scroll padding, causing keyboard focus to disappear behind the navigation bar when tabbing backwards or jumping to anchor links.

metadata.implementation: Create semantic aliases for base colors (e.g., --color-error: var(--red-9), --color-success: var(--green-9)). Apply these semantic tokens to UI components instead of raw color names or hex codes.
metadata.detect: Scan CSS/styled-components for semantic token usage (e.g., color: var(--color-error)) instead of hardcoded hex values or base color names (e.g., color: red).
metadata.anti_pattern: Hardcoding hex values (#FF0000) or using base palette names (--red-500) directly in component styles for stateful or meaningful UI elements.

metadata.implementation: Define design tokens using semantic naming conventions (e.g., 'color-feedback-error', 'color-feedback-success', 'color-action-primary') instead of literal color names. Map base palette colors (e.g., 'red-500') to these semantic tokens, and only use the semantic tokens in component styles.
metadata.detect: Scan CSS/SCSS/JS theme files for semantic token definitions. Lint component styles to ensure no hardcoded hex values or literal color tokens (e.g., 'color-red') are used directly on elements like alerts or buttons.
metadata.anti_pattern: Hardcoding hex values in component styles or using literal color tokens (e.g., 'bg-red-500') for decorative purposes where the color implies a specific feedback state.

metadata.implementation: Map raw ML probability scores to semantic labels (e.g., >80% = 'High Match', 50-80% = 'Possible Match') and pair them with actionable UI elements (e.g., 'Review' or 'Approve' buttons) instead of displaying raw percentages.
metadata.detect: Inspect UI components displaying ML predictions for semantic text labels or color-coded badges rather than raw percentage strings (e.g., '87.4%').
metadata.anti_pattern: Displaying raw probability scores like 'Confidence: 92.3%' to non-technical end users without explaining what the score means or what action they should take.

metadata.implementation: Abstract base palette colors into semantic intent tokens (e.g., --color-error-*, --color-success-*, --color-info-*). Apply these intent tokens to components based on their functional meaning rather than visual appearance.
metadata.detect: Scan component stylesheets for semantic token usage (e.g., var(--color-error-main)) and flag direct usage of base palette tokens (e.g., var(--red-500)) or hardcoded hex values.
metadata.anti_pattern: Using brand colors for destructive actions, or hardcoding hex values like #FF0000 for error states instead of using a semantic token.

Apply these semantic tokens to UI components like alerts, badges, and validation messages instead of using base palette colors.
metadata.detect: Analyze component stylesheets for the use of semantic status tokens (e.g., var(--color-error)) and flag the direct use of base palette colors (e.g., var(--red-500)) or hardcoded hex values.
metadata.anti_pattern: Applying var(--red-500) directly to an error state, which breaks themeability and semantic meaning.

metadata.implementation: Create semantic alias tokens (e.g., color-intent-danger, color-intent-success, color-intent-info) that map to the core color palette. Apply these intent tokens to status badges, alerts, and validation messages instead of raw color names.
metadata.detect: Scan CSS/styled-components for semantic token names (e.g., var(--color-danger)) in alert or validation components. Ensure raw colors (e.g., red, #FF0000) are not hardcoded.
metadata.anti_pattern: Hardcoding hex values or using generic color names (e.g., color: var(--red-500)) directly in UI components for status indicators.

metadata.implementation: Place the highest priority links (e.g., 'Home', 'Dashboard') at the far left or top of a navigation sequence, and the primary call-to-action or utility (e.g., 'Checkout', 'Logout') at the far right or bottom. Put lower-priority links in the middle.
metadata.detect: Analyze the DOM order of navigation lists (<nav> ul li). Verify that primary CTAs or high-traffic links occupy the first and last indices of the list.
metadata.anti_pattern: Burying the primary 'Save', 'Checkout', or 'Submit' button in the middle of a row of secondary actions.

metadata.implementation: Order navigation menus or action lists so the highest-priority items are first (left/top) and the next most important (like 'Save' or 'Profile') are last (right/bottom). Place less frequently used items in the middle.
metadata.detect: Analyze navigation arrays or flexbox layouts to ensure primary CTAs or key links are at index 0 or the final index.
metadata.anti_pattern: Burying the primary 'Checkout' or 'Submit' action in the middle of a row of secondary buttons.

metadata.implementation: Use JavaScript to evaluate complex logic (e.g., matching passwords). Call 'inputElement.setCustomValidity("Error message")' if invalid, or 'inputElement.setCustomValidity("")' if valid, to hook into the native browser validation UI and block submission.
metadata.detect: Search the codebase for '.setCustomValidity(' calls attached to form input validation logic.
metadata.anti_pattern: Reinventing native validation tooltips from scratch or failing to block form submission when custom JS validation fails.

metadata.implementation: Apply identical visual traits (border-radius, padding, typography, and background color) to a group of related secondary actions, such as a rich text editor toolbar or a set of filter chips, to signify they belong to the same functional category.
metadata.detect: Verify that sibling interactive elements within a specific control group share the same CSS classes or design tokens for shape, size, and color.
metadata.anti_pattern: Mixing button shapes (e.g., pill and square) or randomizing colors within a single cohesive toolbar or filter group.

metadata.implementation: Place a single text search input and 1-3 primary dropdown filters directly above the table. Avoid using a dedicated left-sidebar with multi-select facets unless the dataset exceeds thousands of rows with complex dimensions.
metadata.detect: Check for a filter bar above the table (<input type="search"> or <select>) and ensure there is no complex faceted sidebar (<aside> with multiple checkbox groups) for simple datasets.
metadata.anti_pattern: Implementing a full e-commerce style faceted sidebar for a simple 50-row admin data table.

metadata.implementation: Use CSS Flexbox ('flex-direction: column') or block-level display to stack form fields vertically. Ensure each field and its label occupy their own horizontal row.
metadata.detect: Analyze CSS styles on the form container for vertical stacking properties (e.g., 'display: flex' with 'flex-direction: column', or inputs set to 'display: block' with 100% width).
metadata.anti_pattern: Using multi-column grids for sequential form fields, which disrupts the user's vertical scanning flow and increases cognitive load.

metadata.implementation: Style form groups with `display: flex; flex-direction: column;` or CSS Grid with a single column (`grid-template-columns: 1fr;`) to stack fields vertically. Limit multi-column rows to highly related short fields (e.g., First/Last Name).
metadata.detect: Inspect the CSS layout of the form container. Verify that primary form fields stack vertically rather than sitting side-by-side in multiple columns.
metadata.anti_pattern: Using a multi-column grid (e.g., 2 or 3 columns) for sequential form fields, causing a zig-zag reading pattern that slows down completion.

metadata.implementation: Pre-populate form fields using known user data, contextual defaults (e.g., current date, detected location), and provide autocomplete suggestions for text inputs.
metadata.detect: Verify that forms utilize standard HTML 'autocomplete' attributes, default values are set for common selections, and previously entered data is carried over.
metadata.anti_pattern: Requiring users to re-enter their shipping address when it matches their billing address, or leaving common fields blank when the system already has the data.

metadata.implementation: Pre-fill form fields based on known user data or context (e.g., auto-selecting the user's country based on IP, defaulting to standard shipping). Use address autocomplete APIs and standard HTML autocomplete attributes to reduce typing.
metadata.detect: Check for defaultValue or value props populated from user context. Look for autocomplete attributes on inputs (e.g., autocomplete="shipping address-line1").
metadata.anti_pattern: Forcing users to manually type out their full address, country, and state every time without any suggestions, pre-filled data, or HTML autocomplete tags.

metadata.implementation: Pre-populate form fields using known user data, geolocation, or the most statistically common selections. Utilize standard HTML autocomplete attributes to allow browsers to fill in repetitive data.
metadata.detect: Verify the presence of valid 'autocomplete' attributes on standard inputs (e.g., autocomplete="shipping address-line1") and pre-filled 'value' attributes based on user context.
metadata.anti_pattern: Forcing users to manually re-enter data (like shipping address or email) that they have already provided in previous steps or sessions.

metadata.implementation: Instead of immediately destroying data or asking for a disruptive confirmation modal for every action, temporarily hide the item and show a toast notification with an 'Undo' button. If not undone within a timeframe (e.g., 5-10 seconds), commit the deletion.
metadata.detect: Look for toast/snackbar components containing an 'Undo' action triggered after a delete operation, and verify data is preserved in state until the timeout.
metadata.anti_pattern: Clearing a massive form on a single accidental click of a 'Reset' button without confirmation or undo.

metadata.implementation: Place primary navigation in expected locations: at the top (header) or left side (sidebar) of the screen. Use universally recognized icons (e.g., a magnifying glass for search, a hamburger icon for mobile menus, a gear for settings) to match user mental models.
metadata.detect: Verify the placement of the <nav> element in the DOM (top or left). Check icon usage against standard libraries and conventions.
metadata.anti_pattern: Placing the main navigation menu at the bottom right of a desktop screen or using abstract, non-standard icons for common actions like 'Search' or 'Home'.

metadata.implementation: Place primary navigation in expected locations: top header (horizontal) or left sidebar (vertical). Use standard icons (e.g., magnifying glass for search, hamburger for mobile menu, shopping cart for checkout).
metadata.detect: Verify <nav> elements are positioned at the top or left of the viewport using CSS (e.g., top: 0, left: 0). Check for standard ARIA labels and common SVG icon usage.
metadata.anti_pattern: Placing the main navigation menu at the bottom right of a desktop screen or using abstract, non-standard icons for common actions.

metadata.implementation: Place primary navigation at the top or left side. Put the logo in the top-left (linking to home), search bar in the top-center, and user profile/cart in the top-right. Use standard icons (e.g., magnifying glass for search, hamburger for mobile menu).
metadata.detect: Analyze DOM structure for standard semantic tags (<nav>, <header>) and verify placement of logo, search, and cart/profile via CSS positioning or layout grids.
metadata.anti_pattern: Placing the main navigation menu at the bottom of a desktop screen or using abstract, non-standard icons for common actions like search or settings.

metadata.implementation: Design dropdowns and cascading menus with wide hover tunnels and implement a slight delay (e.g., 300ms) or directional aiming detection (SVG triangle method) before closing the menu when the cursor strays outside the strict path.
metadata.detect: Check menu components for 'setTimeout' on 'mouseleave' events or logic calculating cursor trajectory.
metadata.anti_pattern: Cascading menus that instantly close the moment the cursor leaves the exact 1px boundary of the parent item.

metadata.implementation: Design nested dropdown menus with a 'safe triangle' (SVG overlay or JS delay) or increase the vertical height of menu items to widen the 'tunnel', preventing accidental menu closure when moving the cursor diagonally.
metadata.detect: Check if nested menus remain open for a short delay (e.g., 300ms) when the cursor leaves the parent item, or if a directional aiming triangle is implemented.
metadata.anti_pattern: Nested menus that close instantly the millisecond the cursor strays 1px outside the horizontal path.

metadata.implementation: Break complex setup tasks into a linear sequence of distinct screens (a wizard). Include a progress indicator (e.g., 'Step 1 of 4' or a visual stepper), clear 'Next' and 'Back' navigation, and group related inputs logically per step to reduce cognitive load for novices.
metadata.detect: Look for a multi-step form component (e.g., `<Wizard>` or `<Stepper>`) with a progress bar and sequential navigation controls during the initial user setup phase.
metadata.anti_pattern: Presenting a massive, single-page scrolling form with dozens of fields for a first-time user setup.

metadata.detect: Look for a multi-step layout component containing a progress bar or stepper, isolated form sections per view, and sequential navigation controls.
metadata.anti_pattern: Presenting a massive, single-page scrolling form for initial account setup, or forcing users into a rigid wizard for daily, repetitive data entry tasks.

metadata.implementation: Break complex workflows into discrete steps using a wizard/stepper component. Always provide a 'Back' or 'Previous' button that preserves previously entered data, allowing users to review and reverse their actions at their own pace.
metadata.detect: Verify the presence of 'Back' buttons in multi-step forms and check that state management retains input values when navigating backwards.
metadata.anti_pattern: Forcing users through a multi-page flow where hitting the browser 'Back' button loses all entered data.

metadata.implementation: Place primary Call-to-Action buttons at the bottom-right (for Z-pattern layouts like landing pages) or bottom-left (for F-pattern layouts like text-heavy forms) of a content block, ensuring it sits at the natural terminus of the user's reading path.
metadata.detect: Check DOM structure to ensure the primary CTA button is the last interactive element within its parent container and is aligned to the appropriate side (e.g., using flexbox 'justify-content: flex-end' for Z-pattern).
metadata.anti_pattern: Placing the primary CTA at the top right of a text-heavy article before the user has read the context, or floating it randomly in the middle of a paragraph.

metadata.implementation: Define a design system color palette using CSS variables where text colors are pre-validated to meet 4.5:1 contrast against their designated background tokens.
metadata.detect: Run automated accessibility linters (like axe-core) to compute contrast ratios of text nodes against their backgrounds.
metadata.anti_pattern: Using light gray text on a white background for secondary information, resulting in a contrast ratio below 4.5:1.

metadata.detect: Inspect network request wrappers or UI state logic for timers that trigger different loading components (spinner vs. progress bar) based on elapsed time or expected duration.
metadata.anti_pattern: Freezing the UI without any visual feedback for a 5-second API call, or showing an infinite spinner for a 2-minute file upload.

metadata.implementation: When a user performs a state-changing action (e.g., delete, archive), execute it optimistically but display a temporary toast notification (e.g., 5-10 seconds) with a clear 'Undo' button to reverse the action, keeping the user in control of the pace and final outcome.
metadata.detect: Look for toast or snackbar components containing an onClick handler labeled 'Undo'. Verify the action is reversed in the application state when clicked.
metadata.anti_pattern: Using blocking confirmation modals for easily reversible actions, or providing no immediate way to reverse an accidental click.

metadata.anti_pattern: Small icon buttons (e.g., 24x24px) with no padding, placed close together, leading to accidental taps.

metadata.implementation: Ensure all interactive elements (buttons, links, icons) have a minimum bounding box of 44x44 CSS pixels. Use CSS 'padding' or 'min-width'/'min-height' to expand the clickable area even if the visual icon is smaller.
metadata.detect: Inspect DOM elements with click/touch event listeners to ensure computed 'width' and 'height' are >= 44px.
metadata.anti_pattern: Using 16x16px icon buttons with no padding, placed closely together.
